title: Five Teams, One Spot: The Maths Behind IPL 2026’s Most Dramatic Playoff Race in Years
excerpt: After Sooryavanshi’s Jaipur blitz, Rajasthan hold their fate — but Punjab, CSK, KKR and Delhi all cling to mathematical life. Here is how the final six matches will determine the last knockout berth.
body:
Five teams. One spot. Six matches to go. And every result from here could knock somebody out.

The Math After Jaipur

Rajasthan Royals' seven-wicket demolition of Lucknow Super Giants on Tuesday night — powered by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's blistering 93 off 38 balls — has redrawn the IPL 2026 playoff picture in the starkest possible terms. With Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Gujarat Titans, and Sunrisers Hyderabad already confirmed for the knockout rounds, exactly one berth remains, and five franchises still harbour mathematical hope of claiming it.

Here is where things stand after 64 of 70 league matches:

| Team | P | W | L | Pts | NRR | Games Left | |------|---|---|---|-----|------|------------| | Rajasthan Royals | 13 | 7 | 6 | 14 | +0.083 | 1 (vs MI, May 24) | | Punjab Kings | 13 | 6 | 6 | 13 | +0.227 | 1 (vs LSG, May 23) | | Chennai Super Kings | 13 | 6 | 7 | 12 | -0.016 | 1 (vs GT, May 21) | | Delhi Capitals | 13 | 6 | 7 | 12 | -0.871 | 1 (vs KKR, May 24) | | Kolkata Knight Riders | 12 | 5 | 6 | 11 | -0.038 | 2 (vs MI May 20, vs DC May 24) |

Rajasthan Hold Their Own Destiny

The Royals are in the most comfortable position of the five. A win against Mumbai Indians on May 24 takes them to 16 points — a total no other chaser can match. Even a defeat leaves them on 14, which could still be enough if Punjab stumble against the eliminated Lucknow Super Giants a day earlier.

The key asymmetry: Rajasthan play last. They will know Punjab's result before walking out at Wankhede. If Punjab lose on May 23, Rajasthan qualify regardless of their own result. It is the kind of cushion that lets a team play without desperation, which, in tournament cricket, is often the decisive advantage.

Punjab Kings: Win and Wait

Punjab's equation appears simpler but hides a trap. At 13 points with one match remaining, beating Lucknow would take them to 15 — enough to qualify if Rajasthan lose to Mumbai. But if both Punjab and Rajasthan win, the Royals finish on 16 and Punjab go home despite a superior net run rate.

The cruel irony is that Punjab's NRR of +0.227 is the best among the five contenders. If points were equal, they would sail through. But Rajasthan's extra game in hand means points are unlikely to be equal — the Royals either surge ahead to 16 or stand pat on 14, making Punjab's NRR advantage irrelevant in both scenarios.

CSK and Delhi: Hope as a Mathematical Concept

Chennai Super Kings, sitting on 12 points after their Chepauk heartbreak against Sunrisers, face Gujarat Titans on May 21. Even a win only takes them to 14. Qualification requires Rajasthan to lose and Punjab to lose — an increasingly improbable parlay. MS Dhoni's farewell season, if this is indeed it, now hinges on two other teams failing.

Delhi Capitals are in the same 12-point bracket but carry a net run rate of -0.871, which functions less like a number and more like an anchor. Their path requires winning against KKR on May 24 and then watching every other mid-table contender collapse. In practice, Delhi's campaign is over.

KKR's Houdini Act

Kolkata Knight Riders possess the most interesting mathematical profile: 11 points but two matches remaining. Wins over Mumbai Indians (May 20) and Delhi Capitals (May 24) would give them 15 points. They would then need Punjab to lose to Lucknow and Rajasthan to lose to Mumbai — essentially requiring the entire mid-table to self-destruct.

It is the sort of scenario that WhatsApp cricket groups will diagram on napkins for the next five days. It is also the sort of scenario that almost never materialises.

The Diaspora Angle

For the millions of NRI fans who set alarms for 6 AM IST starts, the final week is appointment viewing. The May 23-24 doubleheader weekend — Punjab vs Lucknow followed by KKR vs Delhi and Mumbai vs Rajasthan — is effectively a four-team sudden-death tournament compressed into 36 hours.

Streaming platforms JioHotstar (India) and Willow TV (North America) will carry every ball. In living rooms from Edison to Southall to Brampton, the debates have already begun: is Sooryavanshi's 93 the innings that sealed the fourth spot, or will Punjab's superior NRR rescue them at the death?

The answer arrives this weekend. Set your alarms accordingly.
